title: Measuring ROI on AI-assisted development
question: What does AI-assisted development cost, what value does it deliver, and can we credibly attribute the difference?
summary: ROI requires both the incremental cost of AI-assisted work and its incremental value against a comparable baseline. Local Copilot stores report consumption and some work context, not monetary cost, developer time saved or delivered value. The live measurements below show how much reported usage can be linked to work; they are ROI readiness indicators, not ROI. A deterministic PR join, verified delivery and quality outcomes, billing and human effort data, and a comparable baseline are needed before calculating a return.

tiers.name: Native
tiers.method: Work ownership emitted by the surface
tiers.example: Cloud-owned session → PR; audit agent_session_id. A mentioned session_refs PR is only a reference until verified.

tiers.name: Deterministic
tiers.method: Exact, unambiguous join on VCS keys
tiers.example: Match head repository, commit and time to a verified PR. Branch reuse, forks and multiple PR matches require explicit disambiguation.

tiers.name: Inferred
tiers.example: Same repo and actor inside the PR commit window; modified files ∩ PR diff

tiers.name: Allocated
tiers.example: Org day/user/model credits distributed by attributed local share

tiers.name: Unattributed
tiers.example: Never dropped, so coverage stays visible

invariants: Count each model call once, by stable call ID. VS Code uses chat credits; CLI OTel guidance uses root invoke_agent nano_aiu totals. Never add parent and child totals; validate mappings per surface/version.
Never sum overlapping sources; use precedence, or conservative per-dimension max only for aligned scopes/windows, and record coverage and source.
Unknown is not zero; report credit coverage alongside credit totals.
Credits = nano-AIU / 1,000,000,000; no token-to-currency estimate without an explicit, labelled rate.
Attribution weights per session sum to at most 1; the remainder stays unattributed.

Local observations are not a bill. Reconcile matching consumption with gross AI-credit quantities from the billing AI-credit report, preserving scope filters; show discounts and net billed amounts separately.
No prompt or response content; pseudonymise actors; keep MCP names hashed unless governed.
Never present credits, cache ratios or PR references as monetary ROI or proof of value; report cost, outcome and baseline coverage separately.
Token fields are nullable reported subtotals with per-field call coverage. Cache-read share uses only paired, valid input/cache counts; unknown never becomes a measured zero.

reconciliation.source: Billing AI-credit usage REST: /organizations/{org}/settings/billing/ai_credit/usage or the applicable enterprise/personal endpoint. Not connected by this canvas.
reconciliation.grain: Billing entity × UTC day × user × product/SKU × model; preserve the request filters because usageItems do not carry every dimension.
requirements: Organisation ai_credits_used is user-level consumption, not invoicing and not a model/feature/surface breakdown; reconcile it only at its published grain.
Use the billing entity that pays for the seat. Personal endpoints exclude organisation-managed seats; organisation/enterprise access requires the appropriate administrative permissions.
Match user identity, UTC date, model aliases, product/SKU, unitType and observed coverage. Compare local credits with gross AI-credit quantity only when those scopes align.
Keep gross, discount and net quantities/amounts separate. The documented nominal rate is USD 0.01 per AI credit, not proof of an incremental charge after allowances and discounts.
Store filters and returned scope metadata, retrieval time, coverage and a stable ledger key. Do not add overlapping per-day/user/model queries or duplicate local sources.
Report signed differences and unmatched usage explicitly. Include seats, Actions/infrastructure and human oversight separately before valuing an investment.
reconciliation.allocationPolicy: User/day/model or work-item allocation is T3 estimation, not measured per-session billing. Preserve missing local/cloud usage and unallocated balances; never manufacture per-model usage from ai_credits_used.

outcomes.name: PR-reference coverage
outcomes.measure: % of reported credits in sessions with a repository, branch and recorded PR reference; not verified delivery or value

outcomes.name: Work-context coverage
outcomes.measure: % of reported credits on model calls with resolved repository context, including trace-only links; not verified work ownership

outcomes.name: Credit coverage
outcomes.measure: % of model calls that report credits

outcomes.name: Actor coverage
outcomes.measure: % of reported credits on model calls attributed to a user.name (opt-in identity capture); a join key to per-user organisation data, not a productivity measure

outcomes.name: Cost per delivered change
outcomes.measure: Credits per merged PR, per work-item type

outcomes.name: AI-assisted share
outcomes.measure: % of merged PRs with T0/T1 attribution

outcomes.name: Cache-read share
outcomes.measure: Cache-read / input tokens over calls reporting both valid counts, with paired-call coverage; usage mix, not time or money saved

outcomes.name: Speed
outcomes.measure: Local latency/TTFT fields exist but are not rendered here; PR lead time vs a matched baseline needs verified PR data

outcomes.name: Quality
outcomes.measure: Acceptance/survival require the telemetry feed this canvas does not read; reviews, CI, reverts and verified task delivery require external joins

outcomes.name: Billed AI cost
outcomes.measure: Match reported consumption with billing gross AI-credit quantity at the same user/day/model scope; retain discounts/net billed amounts, seats and infrastructure separately

outcomes.name: Human effort and rework
outcomes.measure: Developer time spent prompting, reviewing, correcting and maintaining delivered work vs comparable non-AI work

outcomes.name: Incremental return
outcomes.measure: (Valued incremental benefit − AI investment) / AI investment; include incremental spend and oversight, avoid double-counting time savings, and use a comparable baseline

gaps.title: No reliable PR / issue ID locally
gaps.consequence: Consumption stops at branch/commit: VS Code emits no work-item ID, and CLI/app session_refs capture one only when the agent references it.
gaps.mitigation: Resolve (repo, branch) and (repo, commit) to PRs through the GitHub API; adopt vcs.change.id.

gaps.title: No verified per-session cloud cost export
gaps.consequence: The billing unit is documented, but PR-linked sessions have no cost source connected here.
gaps.mitigation: Verify a session usage export; otherwise use billing AI-credit reports with labelled T3 allocations and an unmatched balance.

gaps.title: No session ID in organisation data
gaps.consequence: Per-user ai_credits_used has no model/surface split and cannot join to sessions.
gaps.mitigation: Reconcile user/day consumption at its own grain; use filtered billing AI-credit reports for user/day/model and label any allocation T3.

gaps.title: No verified local login join by default
gaps.consequence: CLI/app rows hold no user and their OTel pseudonym is not a verified login; VS Code user.name is opt-in and its user_login equivalence remains unverified.
gaps.mitigation: Verify the opt-in VS Code user.name to user_login join; use a governed identity mapping or collector-supplied login for CLI/app, and pseudonymise before storage.

gaps.title: Session ID missing on many VS Code calls
gaps.consequence: Native session identity is incomplete even when trace-only work context can be resolved.
gaps.mitigation: Resolve time-appropriate session, conversation, parent-session or trace context; do not fabricate sessions, and retain unmatched calls.

gaps.title: Overlapping sources
gaps.consequence: Double counting (metrics vs spans, transcript vs trace, CLI store vs OTel), or undercount with mismatched scopes.
gaps.mitigation: Use precedence or conservative max only for aligned scopes/windows; dedupe call IDs and never sum parent and child usage.

gaps.title: No CI/CD linkage
gaps.consequence: Build and deploy outcomes are unattributed.
gaps.mitigation: Join cicd.pipeline.run.* by repository and commit.

gaps.title: Credits optional on spans
gaps.mitigation: Track credit coverage; prefer the session store or transcript.

gaps.title: MCP server name hashed by default
gaps.consequence: Vendor-level tool cost needs content capture.
gaps.mitigation: Keep the hash as key; map names in a governed lookup.

gaps.title: Naming drift
gaps.consequence: github.copilot.git.* vs vcs.*; reasoningEffort vs gen_ai.request.reasoning.level.
gaps.mitigation: Normalise to canonical fields at ingest.

priorArt.name: bear-in-mind
priorArt.proved: Metering from VS Code OTel file feed, agent-traces.db and transcripts; cost/speed/quality dashboard with retained-trace credits by model, repository, user, caller and reasoning effort, and session repository and user labels.
priorArt.learned: Count only chat spans; dedupe by span ID; metrics vs spans use max not sum; credits = nano-AIU / 1e9; token share is not credit share; user.name, like repository, sits on invoke_agent spans and must be inherited by chat spans.

priorArt.name: agentic-sdlc-prototypes-patterns
priorArt.proved: OTLP receiver, CLI session-store ingestion, ELK documents with cost/speed/quality groups, pseudonymised developer_id.
priorArt.learned: Spans rarely carried credits then; the CLI store was the reliable cost source; repository must be copied from invoke_agent to chat spans.

priorArt.name: copilot-insights (hackathon)
priorArt.proved: Relational schema joining OTel spans, metrics and events with CLI llm_calls by session.
priorArt.learned: Repo/branch/commit exist, but no PR join was built.

priorArt.name: vscode-insights (hackathon)
priorArt.proved: Copilot SDK instrumentation (assistant.usage, subagent.*, skill.invoked, quota snapshots) into one records table.
priorArt.learned: Stable call keys like sdk:<sessionId>:call:<apiCallId>; account checked against the signed-in login.

verification.claim: copilot_chat.copilot_usage_nano_aiu is emitted on VS Code chat spans
verification.note: genAiAttributes.ts in microsoft/vscode extensions/copilot; present on 124 of 125 local chat spans.
Defined in current source and observed locally on invoke_agent / execute_tool spans.
Carried inside the copilot_chat.request.options JSON blob, not a dedicated attribute.

verification.claim: VS Code identity capture: user.name on agent invocation spans; process.user.name and host.name as resource attributes
verification.note: VS Code 1.140 release notes and otelIdentity.ts in microsoft/vscode extensions/copilot: off by default; user.name is the GitHub session account label; a managed policy overrides COPILOT_OTEL_CAPTURE_IDENTITY and the setting; agent-traces.db persists span attributes only; agent host support is tracked in microsoft/vscode#337413.

verification.claim: VS Code user.name equals the usage metrics user_login
verification.note: Both should be the GitHub login; not tested against an organisation export.

verification.claim: Copilot CLI OTel span, metric and environment-variable names
verification.note: Primary CLI reference documents COPILOT_OTEL_ENABLED, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, COPILOT_OTEL_FILE_EXPORTER_PATH; invoke_agent/chat/execute_tool; gen_ai.* and github.copilot.*. github.copilot.cost is a multiplier; use the documented root-span nano_aiu aggregation, not VS Code's mapping.
Both are service request IDs; equivalence not tested.
Primary usage-based billing docs include cloud agent and define one AI credit as USD 0.01. Premium requests remain for eligible existing annual plans; do not mix billing regimes.
Both are in the primary CLI command reference. They are soft limits, not a hard spending guarantee.

verification.claim: CLI limits reset grain and minimum for the installed runtime
verification.note: The command reference says per response, while the session-limit guide says entire interactive session and a 30-credit minimum. Pin the runtime and verify reset/overshoot behaviour before promising semantics.

verification.claim: Enterprise-managed OTel export and cost-centre budgets
verification.note: Primary OTel and organisation billing docs describe enforced telemetry settings and cost-centre budgets for additional charges after pooled credits are exhausted. This is capability evidence, not verification of an account's configuration.
Billing-unit documentation does not establish a session-ID-bearing usage export; no such source is connected to this canvas.
